raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Apply the existing Linux bundled-OpenMP preload policy to RISC-V CPU workers, consistent with the other supported Linux CPU architectures.

## Claims

- Search PyTorch's `torch.libs` and `torch/lib` directories for bundled libgomp on RISC-V.
- Preserve an explicitly preloaded OpenMP runtime and leave configurations without bundled libgomp unchanged.
- Add real VllmConfig/CpuPlatform configuration regressions and wire the suite into the existing CPU configuration CI job.

## Validation

[Immutable reproduction sources, raw logs and provenance](https://github.com/luke-opus/vllm/tree/aa7fb87226c82d9964d7214dafc35b0adb6acf47/main-integration) compare upstream `e0d00e4b8eb0c89ec30921d0695cfdd409e9c211` with this independent fix. Execution used Ubuntu 24.04 RISC-V Linux/QEMU 11.1.2, RVV VLEN 256 with agnostic lanes filled with ones. This is not native-hardware or upstream-CI evidence.

| Check | Base | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Six real-object preload configuration cases | 2 failed, 4 passed | 6 passed |

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/platforms/test_cpu.py -k riscv_preloads_bundled_openmp
```

[Repository tests](https://github.com/luke-opus/vllm/tree/aa7fb87226c82d9964d7214dafc35b0adb6acf47/main-integration/runtime/runs/main-repository-01) retain the real root conftest and fixtures. The same candidate tests run on the matching base/fixed headers and full libraries, with actual source/DSO paths, live maps and hashes checked. Baseline failures remain failures; there are no selected errors or skips. Actual exits and file/link restoration are independently recorded.

[Complete build records](https://github.com/luke-opus/vllm/tree/aa7fb87226c82d9964d7214dafc35b0adb6acf47/main-integration/build) show 21 production units rebuilt per base/ERF/BF16 variant (63 total), three full links and three real load/new-operator checks, all exiting 0. The 210 oneDNN units were reused after command/header/library identity checks. Identical environment adaptations use the recorded oneDNN declaration include, real LLVM OpenMP and the existing Torch BLAS fallback for the installed OpenBLAS's missing `sbgemm_`; no stub or replacement backend is used.

[Paired real spawned CPUWorker runs](https://github.com/luke-opus/vllm/tree/aa7fb87226c82d9964d7214dafc35b0adb6acf47/main-integration/runtime/runs/main-openmp-model-02) use pinned Pythia-14m BF16 weights, the default StandaloneCPUModelRunner, mp/spawn, TP=1, two prompts/four greedy tokens each and the **same new-main baseline DSO**. Only the exact one-line platform-policy difference changes. Both children shut down and exit 0; all returned outputs, including eight tokens and their logprobs, are exactly equal. The fixed spawned worker starts with the real bundled libgomp in /proc/self/environ; the baseline starts without a preload. Actual worker identity, library maps, thread count and affinity are recorded. This establishes preload inheritance and output preservation, not a reproduced baseline model failure, utilization gain or elimination of multiple OpenMP runtimes. Both runs retain the production oneDNN-to-Torch linear fallback. The first harness attempt failed before worker launch because its Unix IPC temporary path exceeded the system limit. Its failure and restoration records are retained; the successful new attempt only shortens the isolated temporary directory and keeps source, model parameters and assertions unchanged.

**Full manual pre-commit on Linux:** [this exact head's job](https://github.com/luke-opus/vllm/actions/runs/41283200026/job/124779155761) and the pinned baseline independently ran the unchanged official `uvx pre-commit run --show-diff-on-failure --color=always --all-files --hook-stage manual` command. All four source snapshots (base and three independent fixes) passed **33 selected manual hooks each**, with actual exit 0, no failed/skipped selected hooks, and empty final Git status/diff. [Immutable raw artifacts and identity checks](https://github.com/luke-opus/vllm/tree/490b210b51865ab11c10b14c6e0eaeec7820d475/main-integration/fork-precommit) verify the source commit/tree, original config hashes, runner identity and artifact digests. This is supplemental GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64 execution in the fork; it does not replace the upstream self-hosted eligibility gate or RISC-V hardware validation.

Local changed-file hooks, normal commit/sign-off hooks and full strict/API documentation builds passed. [Documentation preview](https://luke-opus.github.io/vllm/64080-main/getting_started/installation/cpu/) contains the default/enablement wording in this head; independent previews do not establish upstream RTD success. [Current-head CI audit](https://github.com/luke-opus/vllm/tree/aa7fb87226c82d9964d7214dafc35b0adb6acf47/main-integration/source/current-head-ci-audit.txt): DCO passed, but the upstream contributor-eligibility pre-run check failed, so format/lint checks were skipped. RTD's pre-run script also stopped on that check before dependency installation or MkDocs execution. CPU CI selection is included, while native RVV execution, upstream CI and the submitting human's review/test confirmation remain outstanding. This remains a draft.

Earlier-base evidence is retained separately in the evidence repository, including its warnings and limitations; it is not counted as execution of this new head.

## Details

RISC-V was absent from the architecture tuple guarding the established Linux preload policy. This adds it without changing library selection or overriding user-selected OpenMP runtimes. The CPU thread-binding FAQ documents the existing policy and source/distribution-build fallback.

Duplicate searches found no open RISC-V preload fix. #52858 changes CMake oneDNN handling; #35910 concerns distro build-library discovery; #51876 does not modify this runtime platform path. The historically referenced PyTorch issue is closed, so this PR makes no claim that its original utilization bug is reproduced on current PyTorch/RISC-V.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex. No human review or complete serving validation is claimed.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Recorded comparisons and their limits are disclosed; native hardware, upstream CI and human confirmation remain outstanding.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Applicable hooks and strict/API documentation builds pass; rendered documentation is updated in this head.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes the summary, evidence, reproduction commands, root cause, tradeoffs and AI disclosure.
</details>

**BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

 ### How to decide `VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND`?
 
+- On Linux, including RISC-V, vLLM adds PyTorch's bundled `libgomp` to `LD_PRELOAD` before spawning CPU workers when it is available. An existing OpenMP runtime in `LD_PRELOAD` is preserved; source or distribution builds of PyTorch without a bundled `libgomp` use their configured runtime.
+
 - Default `auto` thread-binding is recommended for most cases. Ideally, each OpenMP thread will be bound to a dedicated physical core respectively, threads of each rank will be bound to the same NUMA node respectively, and the default reserved CPUs will be kept for other vLLM components. On x86, ARM, and RISC-V, `local_world_size` CPUs are reserved in total, plus one additional CPU per local rank when KV transfer is enabled. If you have any performance problems or unexpected binding behaviours, please try to bind threads as following.
 
 - On a hyper-threading enabled platform with 16 logical CPU cores / 8 physical CPU cores:

 import os
+from pathlib import Path
 from types import SimpleNamespace
 
 import pytest
 import torch
 
-from vllm.config import CacheConfig, KVTransferConfig, VllmConfig
+from vllm.config import CacheConfig, DeviceConfig, KVTransferConfig, VllmConfig
 from vllm.platforms.cpu import CpuPlatform
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("library_dir", "ld_preload", "append_libgomp"),
+    [
+        ("torch.libs", "", True),
+        ("torch/lib", "/opt/lib/libcustom.so", True),
+        ("torch/lib", "/opt/lib/libgomp.so.1", False),
+        ("torch/lib", "/opt/lib/libomp.so", False),
+        ("torch/lib", "/opt/lib/libiomp5.so", False),
+        (None, "/opt/lib/libcustom.so", False),
+    ],
+)
+def test_riscv_preloads_bundled_openmp_for_thread_binding(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+    tmp_path: Path,
+    library_dir: str | None,
+    ld_preload: str,
+    append_libgomp: bool,
+) -> None:
+    monkeypatch.setattr(os, "environ", os.environ.copy())
+    config = VllmConfig(device_config=DeviceConfig(device="cpu"))
+    torch_pkg = tmp_path / "torch"
+    torch_pkg.mkdir()
+    libgomp = None
+    if library_dir is not None:
+        libgomp = tmp_path / library_dir / "libgomp.so.1"
+        libgomp.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        libgomp.touch()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch, "__file__", str(torch_pkg / "__init__.py"))
+    monkeypatch.setattr("platform.system", lambda: "Linux")
+    monkeypatch.setattr("platform.machine", lambda: "riscv64")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(os, "sched_getaffinity", lambda pid: {0, 1}, raising=False)
+    monkeypatch.setenv("LD_PRELOAD", ld_preload)
+
+    CpuPlatform.check_and_update_config(config)
+
+    expected = ld_preload
+    if append_libgomp:
+        expected = ":".join(filter(None, (ld_preload, str(libgomp))))
+    assert os.environ["LD_PRELOAD"] == expected
+
